title: Slabless PAYG baseline hypotheses
content:
Quick brain-dump: exploring a slabless PAYG baseline (no bundle tiers) versus tiny retainers. Goal: simple meter with clear per-token economics, optional session credits as UX smoothing. Notes-to-self, rough math and open questions below.

Assumptions (starting point)
- GPU amortized cost: $1.20 / GPU-hour effective for hosting (after infra efficiencies; includes infra + ops).
- Effective tokens per GPU-hour (mix) = 12M tokens (mixed short/long traffic; optimistic).
- Infra cost per 1k tokens = $1.20 / 12,000 = $0.0001 per token => $0.10 per 1k tokens.
- Additional infra overhead + storage + networking + misc = +30% => $0.13 per 1k tokens.
- SRE + support + product overhead allocated per-usage (amortized) = $0.05 per 1k tokens.
- Total variable cost baseline (VC) = $0.18 per 1k tokens.
- Target gross margin at scale for PAYG = 70% => list price target ~= VC / (1 - margin) = 0.18 / 0.3 = $0.60 per 1k tokens.

Quick sanity check against market comps: top-tier API providers range widely; $0.60/1k is within reason for a high-quality hosted inference product with streaming and SLO. But we want to be competitive for SMBs: consider anchoring at $0.40/1k with commitment options.

Slabless vs slabbed outcomes (pros/cons)
- Slabless (single per-token price): simple, transparent, predictable UX for new users, no weird rounding.
  - Pro: easy to understand, low friction onboarding.
  - Con: heavy users don't get commit discounts; could push big customers to Dedicated.
- Slabbed (tiers/buckets): gives us clean anchoring for discounts as usage scales, but more complexity.

Mini-retainer hybrid idea (UX smoothing):
- Offer PAYG at $0.45/1k as baseline.
- Allow small retainer option: $50/month retainer gives $25 credit + 10% discount on usage beyond credit for next 90 days. Effect: reduces sticker shock for bursty SMBs.
- Another variant: session credits (convert sessions -> credits) for chat apps (convo session = 100 tokens baseline) so UX mapping is easier for product teams.

Example unit-econ scenarios (rounded numbers)
- User A (casual): 100k tokens/mo -> revenue at $0.45/1k = 100 * 0.45 = $45/mo. VC = 100 * 0.18 = $18 -> gross margin = $27 (60%).
- User B (middling): 1M tokens/mo -> revenue = 1000 * 0.45 = $450/mo. VC = 1000 * 0.18 = $180 -> gross margin = $270 (60%).
- User C (scale but still hosted): 10M tokens/mo -> revenue = 10000 * 0.45 = $4,500/mo. VC = 10000 * 0.18 = $1,800 -> gross margin = $2,700 (60%).

Elasticity thoughts
- If price drops to $0.30/1k, margin falls to ~40-50% unless VC drops (needs more batching/caching/quantization wins). Could drive volume but risk dilution.
- Discounts should be structured to preserve unit margin: e.g., committed discount of 30% only if committed usage increases efficiency (dedicated allocation).

Session credit model quick math (chat-first customers)
- Define 1 session-credit = 200 tokens (avg convo across product).
- Map to token price: at $0.45/1k => per-credit price = 200/1000 * 0.45 = $0.09.
- UX: sell 500 credits for $40 (effective $0.08/credit) -> slight discount, simpler billing.
- Check VC: 200 tokens * 0.00018 = $0.036 VC per credit -> healthy margin if priced >= $0.08.

Small-biz starter promotion idea (limited time, test):
- Free $30 credits for first 30 days (equates to ~66k tokens at $0.45/1k). Goal: product-led discovery. Track conversion to paid in 30/60/90 days.

Open questions / experiments to run
- Can we push effective tokens per GPU-hour from 12M -> 15–18M with better batching and short-seq optimizations? That would materially reduce VC.
- How many customers would prefer session credits vs pure token pricing? Survey in onboarding flow (quick A/B).
- What churn impact for micro-retainers ($20–$75/mo) vs pure PAYG? Hypothesis: small retainer increases stickiness for chat apps.
- Should we expose a latency premium (low-latency route priced +20%)? Potential for revenue capture from latency-sensitive customers.

Metrics to track for this model
- Average tokens per customer per month (TPM).
- Mix: % of usage from short sequences (<512) vs long sequences (>2k) — impacts VC.
- Effective cost per 1k tokens over time (measure infra improvements).
- Conversion rate from free credits -> paying customers and AOV.
- Retention curves for retainer vs PAYG cohorts (1/3/6 month).

Decision heuristics (initial)
- Launch slabless PAYG at $0.45/1k with session credit UX and small retainer option.
- Monitor margin, conversion and retention for 6 weeks; if heavy usage from customers hitting >5M tokens/mo, push conversation to Dedicated sales motion.

Notes to self (todo)
- Run a sensitivity table: price vs margin vs required improvement in tokens/GPU-hour to maintain margin at $0.30/1k.
- Wire quick onboarding survey asking "Would you rather buy credits or tokens?" and A/B the landing.
- Add latency-tier option to product roadmap if there is demand signal from enterprise trials.

Rough sensitivity (one-liners)
- If tokens/GPU-hour = 15M, VC per 1k = $1.20/15000*1000 = $0.08 -> with 30% overhead -> ~$0.10 VC -> price $0.35/1k for 70% margin.
- If tokens/GPU-hour = 9M, VC per 1k => ~$0.22 -> price for 70% margin = $0.73/1k (ouch).

Random scribbles
- Maybe offer "session smoothing" where we round up small requests into micro-batches to reduce overhead -> product-level batching? potential to improve VC.
- Consider per-route pricing (higher for re-ranking / classifier routes) but avoid too many SKUs.

References/links to follow up
- Check infra cost breakdown in CONFLUENCE: infra/2025-q4-costs (linked above).
- Jira ticket PRICE-524: frontend for credits UX.

End notes: keep this intentionally rough. Main hypothesis: slabless is a low-friction default; small retainers + session credits provide behavioral nudges without committing to complex tier table. Validate with A/B and a few targeted sales conversations.

-- Ava (brain-dump)
